question: does the raw-paragraph layer lift or hurt product-path retrieval (retrieval precondition of the 0.797 -> >=0.8045 parity target)?
design: product write_text -> orchestrated query, 20 questions seed 17; base = MEMPLEX_RAW_PARAGRAPH_LAYER=0; raw arm measured twice - mixed fusion (same-pool competition) and fallback fusion (paragraphs fill leftover top-k slots only, now the default). Metric session-level gold recall@8.

results.verdict: fallback neutralizes the mixed-pool dilution exactly: the raw layer costs nothing at the retrieval face and keeps its pointer-resolution and verbatim-authority value

findings: Mixed fusion cost -15pp at top-8 (3 down / 0 up); fallback fusion restores parity with base (0.85 = 0.85) - paragraphs backstop thin pools without displacing extraction hits, pinned by a contract test.
The raw layer's product value is therefore: resolvable source_paragraphs, verbatim authoritative storage, and slot-backstop retrieval - with the ranked-pool interference removed by default.
Base arm cross-check: identical 0.85 across C2 probe and both fidelity runs (three independent executions).
honest_reading: n=20 per arm, CI ~+/-14pp; the fallback-mixed contrast (0.85 vs 0.70, same questions, same seeding) is the strongest signal here - a paired within-run difference, not a cross-run claim. Answer-level parity remains the acceptance instrument and reads 0.7569-0.7669 (target not met; see parity-variance-split and po-parity-multi-current manifests).
